extracted.intended_audience: Authors of R packages submitting to the rOpenSci software peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and submitting an R package to rOpenSci for software peer review, covering scope checks, documentation, automated checks, submission mechanics, and the review/response timeline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope / fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Consult rOpenSci policies to see if your package meets criteria for fitting into the suite and does not overlap with other packages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If unsure, open an issue as a pre-submission inquiry to ask if the package is appropriate. Consider adding points about similar packages to your package documentation. The README should enable editors to assess scope without installing the package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not submit multiple packages at once
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not submit several packages at a time: we request you wait until a package has been approved before you submit another one.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit only one package at a time to avoid overloading reviewers and the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance expectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Do you expect to maintain your package for at least 2 years, or to be able to identify a new maintainer?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should be able to commit to maintenance or identify a successor; notify editors immediately if you can no longer maintain the package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of submission / package maturity
rubrics_metrics.description: Your package should be sufficiently mature so that reviewers are able to review all essential aspects, but keep in mind that review may result in major changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider best time in development to submit. We strongly suggest submitting before publishing on CRAN or submitting a software paper, because review feedback may cause major improvements and breaking changes. Do not submit while the package or an associated manuscript is under review at another venue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Responsiveness & respect for reviewers' time
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the time and effort needed to respond to reviews: think about your availability or that of your collaborators in the next weeks and months following a submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers are volunteers; authors should respond in a timely and respectful manner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repostatus and lifecycle badges guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If you use repostatus.org badges (recommended), submit when you’re ready to get an 'Active' instead of 'WIP' badge. Similarly, if you use lifecycle badges, submission should happen when the package is 'Stable'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Badge state signals maturity/readiness for review.

rubrics_metrics.name: README content and accessibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The README of your package should provide enough information about your package (goals, usage, similar packages) for the editors to assess its scope without having to install the package.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive to explain functionality and aims assuming readers have little to no domain knowledge. Clarify all technical terms, including references to other software. The README should make a strong case for the package. Setting up a pkgdown website is recommended for more detailed online assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Documentation and testing of major functions
rubrics_metrics.description: At the submission stage, all major functions should be stable enough to be fully documented and tested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure major functionality is documented and has tests before submitting so reviewers can evaluate essential aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Run automatic checks (pkgcheck) locally
rubrics_metrics.description: All submissions are automatically checked by our pkgcheck system to ensure packages follow our guidelines. All authors are expected to have run the main pkgcheck function locally to confirm readiness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatively use the pkgcheck GitHub Action. If pkgcheck cannot be passed for some aspects, explain reasons in your submission template. See pkgcheck vignette for details of checking environment and how to modify it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pkgcheck GitHub Action & Docker dependencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the pkgcheck GitHub Action to run pkgcheck as a GitHub Action; if your package requires unusual system dependencies for the Action to pass, submit a pull request adding them to the rOpenSci base Dockerfile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow blog post and Packaging Guide references; submitting PRs to base Dockerfile helps ensure CI can run in the checking environment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accompanying manuscript coordination (JOSS / MEE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on timing for submitting accompanying manuscripts to partner journals: JOSS and Methods in Ecology and Evolution (MEE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For JOSS: do not submit to JOSS until after rOpenSci review is over; if JOSS deems in scope, only the short paper will be reviewed. For MEE: submit to MEE only after rOpenSci reviewers have submitted their reviews (either before or after package acceptance). Not all rOpenSci packages meet journal criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission mechanics: issue & template variables
rubrics_metrics.description: Software is submitted by opening a new issue in the software review repository and filling out the template.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The template includes HTML-styled variables (<!---variable-->) used by the ropensci-review-bot; these must be left in place with values filled between start and end markers. Follow the submission template exactly so the bot and editors can process the submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication on GitHub thread
rubrics_metrics.description: Communication between authors, reviewers and editors will first and foremost take place on GitHub so that the review thread can serve as a full record of the review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may contact the editor by email or Slack if private consultation is needed, but do not contact reviewers off-thread without asking them in the GitHub thread whether they agree. Ensure your GitHub notification settings make it unlikely you will miss a comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository branch and URL requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted packages can be hosted in the main/default branch, or any other non-default branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For non-default branches it is encouraged (but not required) to use a dedicated ropensci-software-review branch. When submitting from a non-default branch, the 'Repository' URL in the submission template should be the full URL to the review branch (e.g., https://github.com/my/repo/tree/ropensci-software-review).

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor initial triage timeline and possible outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: An editor will review your submission within 5 business days and respond with next steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor may assign reviewers, request the package be updated to meet minimal criteria before review, or reject the package due to lack of fit or overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer assignment and review timeline
rubrics_metrics.description: If your package meets minimal criteria, the editor will assign 1-3 reviewers who will be asked to provide reviews as comments on your issue within 3 weeks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviews are posted as comments on the GitHub issue thread and time expectations are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response timeline and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: We ask that you respond to reviewers’ comments within 2 weeks of the last-submitted review, but you may make updates to your package or respond at any time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Your response should include a link to the updated NEWS.md of your package. Once the response is committed, submit it using the bot. Ongoing conversations between authors and reviewers are encouraged. An author response example is provided in the guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting re-checks after changes
rubrics_metrics.description: Any time package changes are likely to alter the results of the automated pkgcheck checks, authors can request a re-check with the command '@ropensci-review-bot check package'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the bot command to trigger re-checks so reviewers and editors see updated automated check results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unable to maintain or respond — required actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Please notify us immediately if you are no longer able to maintain your package or to respond to reviews.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will then be expected to either retract a submission, or to find alternative package maintainers. Maintenance issues can also be discussed in the rOpenSci Slack workspace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repository transfer after approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Once your package is approved, rOpenSci will provide further instructions about the transfer of your repository to the rOpenSci repository.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow subsequent instructions from rOpenSci staff for the transfer process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Code of conduct requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Our code of conduct is mandatory for everyone involved in our review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere to the rOpenSci code of conduct in all interactions during the review.
